title: High Strength and Fracture Resistance of Reduced-Activity W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr High-Entropy Alloy for Fusion Energy Applications.

recollection.starting_material: Elemental powders or ingots of W, Ta, Ti, V and Zr chosen for their low-activation isotopes (a ‘reduced-activity’ refractory high-entropy alloy composition).
recollection.intervention: Likely produced by vacuum arc-melting (or powder metallurgy + hot isostatic pressing), followed by homogenisation and possibly thermomechanical processing to refine grains and remove segregation; mechanical testing and microstructural characterization (SEM/TEM, XRD, atom-probe) were then carried out.
recollection.structure: Presumably a single-phase BCC solid-solution matrix, possibly containing a small fraction of nano-scale B2-type or Laves precipitates and a fine equiaxed grain structure that remains stable to >1000 °C.
recollection.mechanism: High strength and toughness would be attributed to severe lattice distortion solid-solution strengthening from the multicomponent refractory mix, combined with precipitation and grain-boundary strengthening; crack-tip plasticity enhanced by Ti/V/Zr lowering the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature and improving fracture resistance relative to pure W.
recollection.results: The alloy likely showed ≈1.3–1.6 GPa yield strength and ≈2 GPa ultimate tensile strength at room temperature, retaining >1 GPa yield strength at 800–1000 °C. Fracture-toughness (K_IC) values on the order of 150–220 MPa·m^0.5 were reported, with a DBTT at least 150–200 °C lower than pure tungsten, demonstrating promise for divertor and first-wall applications in fusion reactors.

score.note: Correctly suggested arc melting and broadly relevant characterization, but added unsupported processing routes and homogenization. The proposed single-phase, fine-grained/precipitate structure is inconsistent with the observed segregated two-BCC-phase dendritic microstructure. The solid-solution/lattice-distortion strengthening and Ti/V/Zr-assisted plasticity interpretation is substantially correct, despite unsupported precipitation and grain-boundary strengthening. The room-temperature yield estimate is close, but tensile framing, high-temperature strength, toughness, and DBTT values are incorrect or unsupported.
